title: Inspect and maintain Platter releases and state
summary: Understand owned release selection, canonical state, readiness, durable holds, exact drain, schema migration, and safe recovery.
use_when: A reader needs installation identity, readiness scope, hold/drain guarantees, maintained migration, or release/schedule recovery.
do_not_use_when: The goal is preparing/sending, direct installer cutover, domain reset, unrelated Weaver cancellation, or implicit dependency upgrades.
outcome: Exact installed program/provider identity, supported state, readiness, and maintained recovery guarantees are understood without starting domain work.
effects: Product and provider files publish through owned selectors as one release. Direct install and recover are refused; use the declared product command through the Cell executor.

Durable owner-keyed holds prevent new mutations while admitted work settles. Drain observes matching requester summaries and can cancel orphaned exact matching work. Migration preserves retained identities and commits its import before hashed legacy cleanup.

Readiness checks do not collect sources, read Vita works, render PDF, submit models, or send. Explicit supplied setup can initialize a missing template or create activation intent; deployment itself prepares no packets and sends no email.

The product deployment command selects program and provider files, then migrates or initializes state, imports explicitly supplied templates, updates executable references and selects its owned daily definition under ordinary admission and activity locks. It invokes no doctor, creates no hold, drains no requester and temporarily disables no binding. Runtime diagnostics and explicit maintenance remain separate.
authority: Platter owns domain compatibility, hold and drain scope, state migration, readiness and its product definition. Cell owns explicit instruction order and command completion. Nucleus owns matching execution and cancellation; Clockwork owns binding activation and incident policy.
success: Deployment completes declared placement and product setup commands while preserving retained state, saved or explicit schedule intent and failure incidents. Completion establishes no application health or future delivery.
failure_and_recovery: A failed instruction retains completed file, migration, configuration and schedule changes. The executor stops and performs no automatic retry, rollback or product recovery. Interrupted commands have unknown effects. Inspect current product state and complete authorized recovery separately from executor reconciliation and acknowledgement. Preserve separately acquired holds.

Old binaries cannot operate schema seven. Binary-only rollback cannot undo migration; select a compatible candidate. Interrupted cleanup requires agreeing source hashes. Completion receipts avoid repeating completed migration.
privacy: Mode-0600 database and private state contain career, resume, packet and send history. Public installation manifests retain file modes, program/provider identity and local paths. Nucleus history and credentials remain separately owned.
does_not_authorize: Model work, sending, domain reset, foreign-hold release, unrelated Weaver cancellation, dependency upgrades, or automatic clearing of Clockwork halts.

consumers.statement: The current user and Cell coordinator inspect and maintain exact Platter program/provider installation and canonical private state.

preconditions.statement: State must use its canonical supported root. Product deployment uses ordinary admission and activity locks; an existing hold can refuse it. The caller selects required dependency updates explicitly. Separately requested owner-scoped migration requires the sole matching durable hold and proved drain.

inputs.statement: Selected committed Cell source, referenced artifacts and explicit missing-template, projects-template or activation settings when desired. Explicit maintenance uses an exact owner and can request a private completion receipt for migration; manifest deployment neither creates nor consumes that product receipt.

outputs.statement: Owned release selectors and file metadata, bounded explicit maintenance/readiness observations and retained transactional migration and hashed source-cleanup evidence.

data_semantics.statement: All durable runtime content/settings/holds live in canonical schema-seven packets.sqlite3. Disposable Ashby cache and renderer files stay outside the database. Nucleus credentials/evidence remain separately owned.
Migration preserves retained state in place; recovery requires a compatible binary. Hold owner identity is durable authority, not a process-liveness inference.

identity_and_units.statement: An opaque UUID identifies a prepared installed release. Its file metadata and public entry mappings locate supplied resources without an integrity claim. Migration retains packet and run IDs, requests, dates, send keys, subject/body, attachment name/order/bytes and acceptance or uncertainty.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Drain reads all matching nonterminal Nucleus job-summary pages for platter/job-packets and intersects Weaver summaries with retained exact Weaver IDs. Each observation is bounded to 60 seconds; failure or incompleteness cannot prove drain.

Doctor checks local state/configured PDF, executable identities, Email byte payload, renderer, compatible Weaver, and strict authenticated Nucleus. It does not establish initialized source libraries or inspect the external binding. State-only reads require no external service/renderer readiness.

access.statement: Current-user owned selectors select CLI, retained installer and Chancery provider through current. The manifest invokes platter-install deploy with JSON artifact paths and product settings; the old adapter phase protocol is retired. Direct install and recover remain unavailable. Product mutations use activity locks and honor existing holds and predecessor gates or runner locks.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: The product deployment command selects program and provider files, then migrates or initializes state, imports explicitly supplied templates, updates executable references and selects its owned daily definition under ordinary admission and activity locks. It invokes no doctor, creates no hold, drains no requester and temporarily disables no binding. Runtime diagnostics and explicit maintenance remain separate.

Schema-one import commits transactionally before hashed cleanup; schemas two through six preserve legacy workflows and ordered selections while advancing to seven. Interrupted cleanup retains originals and exact source hashes. Completion receipts avoid repeating completed migration, including legacy schema-one receipts without reading their former data-copy fields.

The product command captures an existing platter/daily definition and retargets it directly while preserving timers, arguments, environment, paths, failure incidents and saved enabled intent. Optional enabled overrides that intent; omission leaves an absent binding absent. No automatic incident approval or uncertain resend follows.

operational_limits.statement: Maintenance cancels only matching Platter and retained Weaver assignments, not unrelated Weaver work. Candidate checks never start domain work. No state reset, implicit dependency upgrade, accepted resend, or halt clearance is part of installation.
No installation latency, arbitrary incompatible rollback, future support interval, or deprecation window is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Schema seven preserves historical inputs, requests, artifacts, delivery meanings and ordered selected packets independent of attachments. Older binaries cannot operate it. Program selection does not reverse a migration. Failed instructions retain effects; recovery requires explicit product operations with a compatible program.

reliances.statement: Nucleus supplies compatible execution health and cancellation of exact matching orphaned jobs.
Clockwork supplies separately authorized binding activation, runtime history, durable failure halt, and explicit continuation.
Prerequisite probes depend on supported Cast, Annals, Weaver, Email, Nucleus, and local renderer interfaces; unselected installations are not upgraded implicitly.

Cell prepares artifacts and executes explicitly selected ordered instructions, retaining source and request correlation and process outcomes. Platter owns setup, state, maintenance and application recovery. No independent installed Cell executor contract is declared.
Readiness and PDF configuration validation require Tectonic, Python/pypdf, and original template packages/fonts.
